5867.t: From νοέω (noéō, “to intend, to perceive, to see, to understand”) + -μα (-mă).

5852.t: From Proto-Indo-European *morwís (“ant”). Related to Old Armenian մրջիւն (mrǰiwn) and Latin formīca and perhaps Sanskrit वल्मी (valmī).

5870.t: From Proto-Hellenic *ksuyō, from Proto-Indo-European *ksuyéti, from *ksew- (“to scrape, shave, scratch”). Cognate with Latin novācula, saucius, and many others.

5878.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₁eys-, used to form words denoting passion; see also Latin īra (“anger”), Lithuanian aistra (“violent passion”), Avestan 𐬀𐬉𐬴𐬨𐬀 (aēṣ̌ma, “anger”).

5882.t: From οὐρέω (ouréō, “to urinate”). Not related to Latin ūrīna.

5840.t: Possibly an -ός (-ós) agent noun of ὀμείχω (omeíkhō, “to urinate”), used as a vulgar expression, but this is disputed.

5881.t: From οὖσα (oûsă, feminine present participle of εἰμί (eimĭ́, “to be”)) + -ία (-ĭ́ā, abstract noun suffix). Literally, “beingness”.

5885.t: From a petrified case form of Proto-Indo-European *per- (“beyond, across”), originally meaning "other side"; compare πέραν (pérān, “across”).

5865.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₁enos (“that one”), the source of Latin nē (“truly!”), enim (“truly”).

5844.t: The connection with Old Armenian մխեմ (mxem, “to insert; to immerse”) is obsolete and semantically doubtful.

5874.t: From οἶνος (oînos, “wine”) + χοή (khoḗ, “act of pouring”, also “libation (to the dead)”), from the root of χέω (khéō, “to pour”).

5826.t: μετα- (meta-) + ἀνίστημι (anístēmi), itself from ἀνα- (ana-) + ἵστημι (hístēmi).

5820.t: μερίζω (merízō, “to divide”) + -μός (-mós, event or process noun suffix)

5858.t: From Proto-Indo-European *new- (“to nod”). Cognate with Latin nutō (“to nod”), Sanskrit नव॑ते (návate).

5829.t: According to Beekes, from a noun, perhaps *μεῖρος (*meîros), which would agree with Sanskrit मर्य॑ (márya, “young man; suitor; lover”) and Avestan 𐬨𐬀𐬌𐬭𐬌𐬌𐬀 (maⁱriia, “yeoman”), or *μεῖρα (*meîră).

5849.t: Univerbation of μή (mḗ, “so that...not, lest”) + τις (tis, “anyone”).
